query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered suitable for thin-film use, and its expense favors applying it as a protective coating on conventional metals rather than using it in bulk. Earlier studies examined room-temperature wear behavior in relation to coating–substrate combinations, composition, and grain size, but largely addressed the alloy itself or a limited thermal regime rather than the overall wear response of a coating across different temperatures. Under the constraints that FeNiCrCoCu remains a thin protective coating and that high-temperature wear is the target application, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs its overall wear resistance and why? Specify an intervention relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, state the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, connect the hypothesis to prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Pre-oxidizing the FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating at 800 °C under a controlled load will induce the formation of a stable, adherent Cr2O3/spinel oxide layer that enhances overall high-temperature wear resistance compared to an as-deposited coating.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating deposited on a conventional metal substrate (e.g., steel) without prior thermal treatment.
generation.intervention: Apply a pre-oxidation heat treatment at 800 °C under controlled mechanical load to induce oxide formation.
generation.conditions: High-temperature wear conditions (approximately 800 °C) under high normal load simulating real-world operating conditions of protective coatings in high-temperature applications.
generation.structural_mediator: A protective, adherent oxide layer consisting primarily of Cr2O3 with accompanying spinel oxides (e.g., (Fe,Co,Ni,Cu)3O4) formed at the coating surface.
generation.mechanism: The pre-oxidized layer acts as a mechanical barrier and lubricious film, reducing direct abrasive and adhesive contact during wear. This protective oxide layer maintains microhardness and resists surface degradation under high-temperature conditions, thereby improving the overall wear resistance of the thin-film coating.
generation.predicted_outcome: If the hypothesis is correct, the pre-oxidized coating will exhibit a lower wear rate, higher microhardness, and reduced friction coefficient in high-temperature wear tests compared to the untreated baseline. The oxide layer is expected to remain stable and self-regenerate during wear, providing continuous protection.
generation.baseline: As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating without pre-oxidation treatment.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable under high-temperature (around 800 °C) conditions and high normal load environments. The results may vary outside these temperature or load regimes.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvements (e.g., percentage reduction in wear rate) are uncertain without experimental data, and the precise composition and thickness of the oxide layer may vary depending on processing details.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeNiCrCoCu coatings on steel substrates: one set undergoes the pre-oxidation heat treatment at 800 °C under controlled load and the other set remains as-deposited. Subject both sets to identical high-temperature wear tests using abrasive counterfaces under simulated service conditions.
measurements: Oxide layer composition and thickness by XPS/SEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-oxidized coating does not show a statistically significant improvement in wear resistance, microhardness, or friction behavior relative to the as-deposited control, or if no stable protective oxide layer (Cr2O3/spinel) is detected on the treated coating, the hypothesis is falsified.

reading.lever: Pre-oxidize the FeNiCrCoCu coating at 800 °C under controlled load to induce a stable Cr2O3/spinel protective layer.
reading.why: This approach leverages proven oxide-layer formation benefits from related HEA systems to directly address high-temperature wear resistance in thin coatings.
